_doc: Generated from packages/design/tokens/*.css by crates/og-ui/scripts/gen-theme.sh; never edit it by hand.

color._doc: The game components' materials (role.css and the controls dress with them): `glass` a frame's body from its lit top (`-hi`) to its foot (`-lo`), all but opaque (no blur: a backdrop pass per frame costs a software rasteriser seconds), and `plate` a HUD plate's, a little thinner over the scene; `rim` the edge light catches on glass, a tile and a raised control (`-soft` inside a frame, `-strong` under a pointer); `lit` the highlight along a top edge and `lit-soft` the light falling across a face; `shade` and `shade-deep` what a recess and a foot fall into; `tile` a slot's sunken ground and `tile-pressed` it held down; `card` the glass of a card standing in a frame, thin enough that the frame's light shows through it; `raised-hi` to `raised-lo` a control's face that stands up, `raised-hover-*` under a pointer; `glow` and `glow-soft` the primary's light around what is chosen or live, and `select-hi` to `select-lo` the wash across a chosen row: the primary's on a light ground; on a dark one the glass a step lighter, since a pale primary washed over dark glass in linear light is a grey slab (the row's edge carries the primary there). Opaque wherever nothing shows through, since the engine blends in linear light.

controls._doc: The engine's built-in controls' own values (`--<control>-<property>`, docs/ui.md §3.1): what their part rules dress with (each by default a semantic token) and the sizes, ratios and motion their geometry takes (each the number it drew with; og-ui's theme reads them back). A ratio is of the control's own size. `button-pressed-*` is a button held down; `button-selected-*` one that is on (`aria-pressed`: a toggle, a chip).
controls.button-primary-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 var(--color-lit), inset 0 calc(var(--space-md) * -1) var(--space-md) calc(var(--space-sm) * -1) var(--shadow-30), 0 1px 2px 0 var(--shadow-45), 0 var(--space-xs) var(--space-md) calc(var(--space-xs) * -1) var(--color-glow)

density._doc: Compact is the default; data-density="comfortable" on any element switches its subtree; coarse pointers or widths under 768px raise controls to the touch size.

pad._doc: A gamepad across a room (the engine's): larger controls and rows, wider gutters, so a focused control reads from a couch.

derived._doc: Values the engine's default CSS derives from the roles above, per scheme: `tint` is a role at a fraction of its alpha (`--<name>`), `shadow` the inset shadows of controls built on those tints (`--shadow-<name>`), `alias` names kept for documents and the active density's sizes (`--<name>`: `--control-sm/md/lg`, `--row`, `--header`, `--gutter`, `--section` are the input's density, which the engine selects as `--density-active-*`; `--touch-target` the smallest target a finger gets).

elevation._doc: The engine's two drop shadows under content that lifts (`--elevation-raised`: radio cards; `--elevation-floating`: open lists and slider bubbles): offset, blur and the `shadow` colour's alpha, emitted as `0 <y> <blur> 0 <shadow at alpha>`.

filter._doc: What art takes when its subject is out of reach (`--filter-*`): `locked` not yet earned, `spent` used up or defeated.

font._doc: Tracking a style opens its capitals and small labels with.

cjk._doc: Chinese text (any element under lang="zh…"): PingFang and its peers are set at zero tracking, and display steps get looser leading because CJK glyphs fill the em box. build.mjs emits these as overrides of the --text-* variables under [lang|="zh"], restored under any other [lang].

leading._doc: Leading as a ratio of the size, for text a component sizes itself: `flat` a figure or a one-line plate, `tight` a display line, `snug` a wrapped label, `normal` running text.

font.rounded: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Nunito Variable", "Nunito", "PingFang SC", "HarmonyOS Sans SC", "MiSans", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", system-ui, sans-serif

step._doc: Steps in em of the text a part stands in, so a part sized with one follows the player's text scale (the scale's own sizes are px). `md` is the surrounding size. `px` is one CSS px at 100 % text grown by the scale (rem is the body step, 14 px at 100 %), for a part that grows with the text as a whole, such as a HUD slot.

glass._doc: The engine's glass parts (`-og-material`): the saturation their backdrop takes (`dark.glass` remaps it) and the blur each weight uses, by the `vars` material blurs.

glassContrast._doc: Text over glass ([ink, material, what passes under it]): the material's tint mixed over the underlay as CSS mixes it (srgb, the blur leaving a flat underlay as it is), and optionally a fill over that in linear light. #e4e4e4 and #151515 stand for the brightest and darkest scenes (what og-tests' bright-sky and dark glass scenes measure under a text box); glass-thin carries no text.

linear._doc: The translucent fills restated for the engine's UI pass, which blends flat fills in linear light: each the alpha whose linear blend over `over` draws what CSS's blend of the `color` value draws there (a white 13 % over dark glass reads about three times as strong in linear light). The engine draws these; a browser draws `color`.

materialScope._doc: Lenses on Liquid Glass: inside bars and capsules the hover, current and selected fills become the clear control tints of the material they sit on, and the control rim becomes the ringless lens so a selection never draws a second border inside the bar's rim (each key is a semantic colour or shadow, each value the one it takes there). Overlays that carry text (`reset`, glass-thick menus, popovers, dialogs) take the palette back even inside a bar, and solid glass (reduced transparency, increased contrast) keeps the surrounding values.

measure._doc: Panel, column and track widths (`--measure-*`): how wide a block of content runs before it wraps or scrolls.

metal._doc: Award metals (rank 1–3 medals and numerals): highlight, mid, shade stops of one gradient. Material, not text.

motion._doc: Longer than a transition: what loops and long plays take, each named for the loop it was measured on. `turn` a spinner's turn, a flash going out; `pulse` a beat (a timer's last seconds); `flare` a ring thrown from a burst; `ping` a ping going out; `sweep` an indeterminate bar's pass; `breathe` a waiting thing's breath, a shell's flight; `sheen` a light crossing a bar; `drift` a liquid's sway; `fanfare` a reward held on screen; `orbit` a ring's slow turn.

named._doc: The engine's named transitions (`transition: var(--motion-<name>)` in a document, a widget's motion token): each a spring of a perceptual duration and a bounce (0 none, towards 1 more), capped by a style's overshoot; `ui` also sets --motion-ui-easing, its 60 Hz samples.

scale._doc: How far a moment scales: `press` a control going down, `swell` a hover or a selection, `pop` a hit or a reward arriving, `shrink` what leaves; and how low a waiting thing breathes.

spring._doc: Springs as damping ratio (1 = critically damped, below 1 overshoots) and response (seconds to reach the target; not a duration), the parameters Apple ships. build.mjs emits --ease-spring-<name> (a linear() easing), --dur-spring-<name> (its settle time) and --spring-<name>-damping/-response for the runtime spring (ui-svelte motion/spring.ts); Swift gets the pair for .spring(response:dampingFraction:). default: overlays, menus, highlights; sheet: sheets and drawers; momentum: releases that carried velocity (a flick, a throw).

timing._doc: The timing table: what each moment of a UI moves on, by the duration, easing and spring names above (or a number of its own). A style overrides a row in its motion block (docs/ui.md §3.1); the default style takes these. hover: the lift on the spring named and, for a pad's virtual cursor, how much it slows and settles over a control (magnet 0–1). press: the squash in at once, back on a spring of this damping over the duration named. enter and exit: a widget's arrival and departure. cascade: a list's or a panel's children entering one after another, step between them, never spread past cap. toast: in, held (hold; holdDanger for an error), out. screen: a game-screen transition covers then reveals over this many slow durations.

opacity._doc: How strongly a thing shows (`--opacity-*`): `faint` a watermark or an empty slot's mark, `dim` what cannot be used, `muted` what is done or secondary, `soft` what steps back a little; `wash` is how much of a colour a soft wash lays over what is under it (a chart's area, rays of light). A disabled control takes `--state-disabled-opacity`.

role._doc: Materials: the shadows a raised face, a recess and a held control wear, each with its rim as its first layer (a control has no border of its own). `raise` stands up, `raise-hover` lifts under a pointer, `held` sinks; `sunk` is a recess, brighter in its rim under a pointer (`sunk-hover`), ringed in the primary's light when focused (`sunk-focus`).

role.select-row-on-fill: linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(from var(--hud-accent) r g b / 0.34), rgb(14 22 38 / 0.92) 42%, rgb(10 14 24 / 0.74))
role.select-row-on-rim: inset calc(4 * var(--font-step-px)) 0 0 var(--hud-accent), inset 0 var(--stroke-hairline) 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55), inset 0 0 0 var(--stroke-hairline) rgb(from var(--hud-accent) r g b / 0.55)
role.sunk-focus-shadow: inset 0 0 0 var(--stroke-thin) var(--primary), var(--shadow-sunk), 0 0 0 var(--stroke-thick) var(--color-glow-soft)
role.tag-halo: 1.5px 0 0 contrast-color(currentColor), -1.5px 0 0 contrast-color(currentColor), 0 1.5px 0 contrast-color(currentColor), 0 -1.5px 0 contrast-color(currentColor), 1px 1px 0 contrast-color(currentColor), -1px 1px 0 contrast-color(currentColor), 1px -1px 0 contrast-color(currentColor), -1px -1px 0 contrast-color(currentColor)

safeArea._doc: Device safe-area insets (notch, home indicator, rounded corners) as --safe-area-*; index.html sets viewport-fit=cover. @origingame/ui turns them into pt-safe / pb-safe / px-safe / top-safe / bottom-safe utilities (with -<n>: at least n spacing steps, more where the device has an inset).

shadow._doc: What the game components' materials cast (role.css): `panel` under a frame, lit along its top edge; `plate` under a HUD plate over the scene; `raise` a control or card standing up, `raise-hover` it lifted under a pointer; `sunk` a tile's or a track's recess, with the light its lower lip catches; `held` a control pressed in.

size._doc: Icon, avatar and art sizes (`--size-*`); `touch` is the smallest target a finger gets.

state._doc: How a control answers (`--state-*`): `hover-wash` is how far hover (half) and press (whole) move a control's fill towards the ink; `press-scale` what a pressed button or part shrinks to, `control-press-scale` a pressed control row's; `lift` the hover and focus rise; `disabled-opacity` a disabled control's, `touch-disabled-opacity` a disabled on-screen stick, pad or action button's; the focus ring's width and gap outside the part (`-field` for text boxes), the high-contrast outline's width, and each local player's ring and gaps.

stroke._doc: Line widths (`--stroke-*`): material edges, hairline frames, field rims, open triggers, thick marks and the focus ring.
